citations.review_text: Bought it, installed and ran it then it asked for an xbox account sign in to play it, i asked for a refund instead.......
Microsoft account necessary for a solo game ? Really ? :steamthumbsdown: Refund

Why is this game online only??? I paid money to play this single player game and I can't play it on my Steam Deck away from an internet connection? What the FFFF?

And what is up with the account linking? Why do I have to link my microsoft account with my steam account? What happens in my microsoft account gets hacked, will I still be able to play the game I paid for???

Let me get this straight.
I must LINK my Microsoft account to my STEAM account to play a SINGLE PLAYER GAME.....
On top of that.... "Once linkmed, this aciton cannot be reversed."   Yeah.......
Are you going to come after me if I refund the game? Go after my steam library or something?
♥♥♥♥ YOU MICROSHIT. Linking my Steam acct to microsoft for LIFE??? Not happening. You can go monetize someone else steam acct for life.
 
SAD what you think you can get away with. Alt - F4 to get out of the game too? Dont want us to leave? This is a whole nother level of ridiculous. 

REFUNDING

What do you get when you take a beloved game that holds so many memories and is the gold standard for the video game industry, and try to add modern writing, modern monetization, modern gameplay design, and modern game development methodology? You get the ironically named Halo: Campaign Evolved, which should really be named Halo: Campaign Regressed, as there is no evolution over the original or the Master Chief Collection versions of this game. For the TLDR, buy the Master Chief Collection, as it is, in my opinion, a far easier entry point to the series than this is. The only downside is that the graphics may not look as nice in some places, but at least that collection still has most of Halo’s soul, whereas this remake is soulless for reasons I will note below.

Firstly, I do have to ask, why do we have to connect a Microsoft Account to our Steam Account for a single-player game? I do not understand why this was seen as necessary in any way, other than to harvest our data or some other nefarious reason. I kept getting errors 400 or 500, which, from what I've read online, indicate an account session issue or an Xbox Services issue. Why was adding another point of failure necessary to a single-player game?

In terms of pricing, with the premium add-on, which are just skins if that is your sort of thing, it comes out to almost 100 CAD before taxes, and the base game, without any multiplayer, is nearly 70 CAD. This is all for a single-player game. Compared to the entry point of all the games in Halo MCC, they cost 50 CAD, or, for the Halo: Combat Evolved Anniversary Edition, a mere 13 CAD. Who thought these prices were reasonable? 

From a design standpoint, the soul has been unceremoniously ripped out of this remake. You cannot just make a game under the Halo IP without giving it the proper respect it deserves and having it made by people who understand the setting correctly. The game babies you every step of the way, and makes it so that even when you are fighting st…

Forced online auth for a single player game. Doesn't even feel like Halo.
Play the MCC instead. :^)

Some issues with the gameplay, but its mostly ok.

Not a big fan of the direction the writing is going in (at least starting in the new levels). Kinda treats the player like child.

Having to link to a Microsoft account for a campaign only game sucks, not interested.

citations.review_text: Steam really dropped the ball verifying this for Steam Deck. Even on the lowest settings, I have not gotten 15 seconds of gameplay without crashing.
been unable to play the game due to crashes. this is trash and unacceptable. I will get my money back. they will pay.

After over a week, this game is still not playable. The person I want to play this game with cannot launch on their PC. What's the point if I can't play with my friends? Will change review if it gets fixed.

Windows Experience:
It took nearly 4 hours of painstaking troubleshooting work to get it to launch, but Halo has been installed, linked to my Steam account, and finally, FINALLY launches and gets to the title screen without BSODing my Windows 11 rig with an Intel i9 and RTX 5080.  
Unfortunately it remained  troublesome after.  I had to break out the keyboard and mouse anyway because account linking wouldn't work with the onscreen keyboard from the Steam Controller. Also every time I exit the game it crashes Steam.

Amazingly NONE of this is an issue on the Mint box at my desk.  Even though it's a couple years older hardware.  It just fired up and ran.  No issues doing account sign in, no weird video judder during the cinematics.  Just worked.  
UNTIL.... 
Reaching the end of a mission.  Not been able to get to the 3rd mission yet because the game freezes on a black screen and crashes at the end of the 1st and 2nd missions on the Linux box so I'll have to go back to my Windows machine  to progress. Plus, I don't want to play Halo on a handheld.

Final Thoughts: 
I currently only have 108 minutes in actual game time invested.  I'm seriously considering asking for a refund and revisiting it later when bugs have been worked out and maybe it goes on sale.  Shame, because I've never considered asking for a refund before.  Microsoft should be ashamed of …

claims.claim: Reviewers describe heavy stuttering, frame drops, and poor frame rates even when playing on low graphics settings.

citations.review_text: I don't know if I did something wrong on my end, but I ended up refunding the game because it's unplayable. There's stuttering everywhere and constant frame drops, for example, in the first mission, every time I turned a corridor corner, I'd lose 100 fps for 2-5 seconds, making it impossible to play. I tried every fix I could find on YouTube, but nothing worked for me. Too bad, because if the performance had been fine, I would've picked it up anyway, given the ridiculous price, as a long-time Halo fan.

Could have been a good game if they at least optimized it. Struggled to run on my desktop 7900 XTX at 1440p, and also struggled to run on my laptop RTX 5090 (just to test DLSS and frame gen). Both have similar performance, and I had around 50fps on low graphics, which is shocking. So according to Steam hardware statistics, most people will have a hard time running this game.

After an hour of playing at a low framerate,  with enemies getting stuck in walls and other AI bugs, I just refunded the game because I wasn't having very much fun. 

Also, aiming is set to toggle by default (instead of holding to aim) and there's no way to change it. It seems that they tried to give it a hybrid button layout, but what ended up happening is I would tap aim to quickly headshot an elite, but then get stuck in toggle aim because the game thought that's what I wanted.

Performance and gameplay are both clunky. Would not recommend unless it's on sale and you have an RTX 5080 or better.

Pros: NEW HALO REMAKE!
Cons: Its a money grab, unoptimized, and runs like absolute trash. I actually couldnt get past the first level not because I didnt like it but its because the frame rate, the blur, and how funky everything looks. I adjusted everything properly and even allowed my Nvidia to optimize it because I felt like I was doing something wrong but sure enough the ENTIRE thing just runs awful .

Overpriced stuttery mess. I'm running well over the minimum specs and not far below recommended.
4070 Super, Ryzen 5700g, 32gb ram. 
I can run Doom The Dark Ages on high settings with butter smooth performance.
Sure, I don't have the most powerful rig in the world, but even on medium I'm getting really distracting stutter issues. Why they thought UE5 was a good idea (aside from churning out sub contractors that only know how to develop in UE) is beyond me. The fatigue and resentment players have for UE5 is hardly a secret. 

Not a huge fan of the visuals, the cut scenes so far feel clunky and less alive than even Halo 3. That opening cut scene in the new missions where Chief jumps out of the covenant ship, but his character model looks like it just statically drops, was laughable.

This is not worth the price. If it were half the price I'd say give it a go. At full price, no way. If you're interested in this you probably have Halo 1 already in some other form. Stick to that. This isn't a necessary experience.

I was very excited to try and play this game, it looked great, and I've always been a huge halo fan, unfortunately it seems UE5 kind of kills this game, I had non stop stutters, and lag, and less than 30 fps the whole time, on the LOWEST. SETTINGS. I know I by no means have the best pc hardware but it shouldnt literally be UNPLAYABLE because of how terrible the FPS is at the lowest possible settings. Literally all my time was on the menu and Pillar of Autumn. I almost never leave reviews but I've never had such a horrible experience in a game purely due to me not being able to play the game with how absurdly laggy it is.

had to refund it. basically the same as Halo CE, with performance issues. had frame skipping, even at the lowest graphics setting, and i dont have a potato. 
its also free on gamepass.

claims.claim: Reviewers state that the game lacks online or split-screen multiplayer modes.

citations.review_text:
Rough around the edges but a decent reprisal of Halo CE. The bonus missions suck (especially on LASO good LORD), Boarding Action may be the worst Halo level ever made. The game needs some additional polish which is hopefully coming in later patches. 

The game looks very pretty (once you get the settings right) and mostly stays true to the original's art style which Anniversary utterly failed to do. The guns feel really good (especially the assault rifle). By no means a perfect game but overall pretty good. It has inspired me to return to MCC and enjoy the older games as well. Multiplayer is a painful omission and it would be nice to experience the crisp gunplay and weapon sandbox in a multiplayer setting.

Full disclosure I did not get the achievements on Steam. They synced over from the Xbox app after I did them all on Game Pass (real time played is 92 hours).

As someone who was really looking forward to Halo: Campaign Evolved, I have to say I’m pretty disappointed.

I expected a remake that would truly bring the original Halo back to life and make it feel like a genuinely new experience. Instead, much of it feels less impressive than I had hoped. Sure, the graphics have been improved and there are some changes and additions, but something about the atmosphere and the magic of the original game just doesn’t feel the same.

And the biggest thing missing for me is **online multiplayer**. If you’re going to bring back such an iconic game, the least you could do is include a proper online multiplayer mode. It would have added much more content, significantly extended the game’s lifespan, and given players a reason to keep playing after finishing the campaign.

A remake of such an iconic game should make me feel the excitement I felt with the original Halo all over again, but that simply didn’t happen here. Instead of feeling like I’m playing the ultimate version of this classic, there were many times when I honestly felt like I would rather just go back and play the original.

In the end, considering the Halo name, my expectations, and the price, I expected much more. Proper online multiplayer could have at least made this feel like a much more complete package.

**I cannot recommend this game in any way.** In its current state, I simply don’t think there’s enough here to justify buying it, especially when there are better ways to experience Halo.

**4/10**
no split screen coop on PC is laziness and unacceptable, especially by a big publisher. Fix this now.

The UE5 graphics leave much to be desired, not in the sense it's low fidelity, but more like the retro sci-fi inspired art style has been partially butchered and now it looks like every other UE5 game. Looks better than the anniversary version, but that was literally a rush job made by modders and contractors, so the bar was very low. Performance isn't perfect, but I wasn't having too many low fps moments. On the other hand though I was experiencing some noticeable input delay, and while not massively important since the game doesn't require super fast reactions, it still doesn't feel good to play with a delay of any kind. The game has bugs that weren't present in the original, which is just amazing. On Truth and Reconciliation I died from literally nothing like 10 different times, like legit just falling over. No local PvP or online multiplayer either, just Co-op. It's just a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ circus. 

And the point of "it being a good entry for newcomers" is completely bogus, because the MCC is right there, Halo CE is $10 maximum, and on sales you can get the entire collection for even cheaper than that. If somehow OG Halo CE is "too old" for new gamers, then idk man just stop playing games or never go outside of your modern gaming bubble. This game has no right to exist, it's just more 343 contractor sludge. No one working on this is going to be working on the next remake they might make, it's just a revolving door of misused talent at 343. Really a shame, if they actually had better direction and retained their employees, maybe the past 16 years of stewardship from 343/Halo Studios wouldn't be as contentious. 

[EDIT] The game still sold and has more positive reviews than negative, so I'm not understanding why people are so anal in the comments about my negative experience. Maybe stop hinging your personal enjoyment in life on the success of products, of which the quality is entirely out of your control. I promise my negative review isn't going to make your copy of the g…

Game is very undercooked. They definitely released the game early because they didn't want to compete with the release of GTA VI.

Also, if you have Frame Generation turned on it will warp the cutscenes and look really bad. There is also no way to choose what level of Frame Gen you want because they were lazy.

Many other problems with this game, it just feels bad to play. No Multiplayer pvp is very lame too.

The graphics look blurry and bleh, on top of that they chose to charge us $70 for a few meh cosmetics along with a pre-order bonus that has the original outfits from Halo 1. Just bad practices all around.

It is also super obnoxious they didn't include a firefight game mode considering they have co-op, but there is no matchmaking for co-op, it is the same 'invite your friends' co-op mode all the old Halo games had, which sucks. You can't have people just jump in randomly to your game, which I always hated about Halo games. A firefight mode could have really gave this game some life.

I would agree with this review, the AI does suck, it feels bad to fight against. The game runs terribly, even on a 5800X3D 5090 PC at 4K. You need DLSS to run this game decently.. but for some reason the aiming with mouse feels very off, even with mouse acceleration off.

claims.claim: Reviewers criticize the voice acting and dialogue for being mismatched in tone, poorly directed, or unsuited to the scenes.

citations.review_text: The voice acting in this game is some of the most B-Grade quality I have ever heard. It not just that its different, none of the pitch and tone relates to the mood/tension or energy of the scene in almost any instance. It just constantly breaks you out of the immersion, like nails on a blackboard. More than anything this is making me want to stop playing, regardless of the pretty graphics, which by the way, are impressively unoptimized. Everyone deserves to be fired for this failed development. Its obvious almost everything was outsourced.

The core of the game is good but the execution is poor. Bought it and tried playing with a friend and had constant disconnects over multiple attempts during the span of an entire week. 
The main selling point was the revisiting of the old CE campaign but in a new format and with your friends - so why is it that at the launch of the game when people are most excited for this they fail to execute this basic feature. Is multiplayer connectivity such a hard thing to do for a "top tier" game studio in 2026? 

Second of all the quality of the game is dubious - the faces in the cutscenes (Cortana, Jhonson) are weird and distorted/uncanny valley for me. The voice lines are spoken in a way/tone that is mismatched with the situation and the stakes. If you can't re-record in a way that is congruent with the spirit of the original game then just use the original voice lines. 

New additions (sprinting, hit markers, red markers to show off cloaked enemies) should have been options that you can turn on if you can't quite manage the game in its "original state" but should not have been made the default. 
Lastly some characters (the ODST lady) seem out of place - though I understand there is animosity between SPARTAN IIs and ODSTs that does not mean the portrayal of it was appropriately done or well included into this game. 
I could go on about other issues but I think this has been stated enough - my conclusion is this - the game is not a complete failure because in a lot of places it sticks to and copies what was already an amazing game when it came out and thus this means that they couldn't "fail too much at it". The parts where 343/halo studios deviated from the original or added their own contribution are not coincidentally the weakest parts. 

Ultimately I think what happened to this Halo game is what happens when a developer - Halo Studios/343 Industries is filled with people that have no passion for what they're doing and simply try to make a game "by the numbers". You can …

I've read a lot of reviews of people having issues with the changes to the story and I would like to agree with them. The only thing stopping me is I can't really pay attention to the story to notice the changes because the gameplay is just awful. Guns don't feel weighty or have that "punch" as the original CE or even other Halo games. The brutes are some of the most boring and frustrating enemies to fight. Just bullet sponges for the sake of absorbing damage that give zero feedback to being shot. The game feels half-baked with so many things left unfinished. I'm convinced, truly from experiencing the game myself and not outside sources, that Halo Studios used AI to create a lot of the cutscenes within the game. It's as if it was used to give a baseline for developers to then go back and polish the scenes, but the polishing was never put through quality control. The voice acting feels lifeless and almost forced at times. It's hard to be mad, and I even pre-ordered the game, when all I really feel is just sheer disappointment. Well time to go play the Original or even Anniversary.

Only played the first two missions, and that’s all I needed to see to know this was a shell of greatness. They changed items that had no reason to be changed. The cutscenes, while they look beautiful, lack anything in audio. The first cutscene when you enter the bridge is a jarring rigid transition compared to the original, no alarms in the background, no chatter of marines, it sounds like everyone is in a sound booth. Honestly the audio engineering is disappointing. Voice acting just sounds rushed and isn’t blended into the game well at all. The iconic sound of the banshees flying in on the second mission is completely gone. That was dare I say an iconic part of that mission. 

For a game that was supposed to “evolve” the campaign, it’s a stark let down and a downgrade from the anniversary edition. Just play the anniversary edition instead.

TLDR: another L take from 343. Disappointing to see them fumble yet again with the Halo franchise, especially on a project where they had a literal blueprint.

Look how they massacred my boy

The whole tone is completely lost with the new dialogue. The serious tone is gone - this has ruined the game for me. The ODST chick they added in the new missions is insufferable with no dimension at all, a "girl boss" who's unnecessarily confrontational and arrogant. Johnson is too jovial as well. He was originally serious but a wise-cracking action man. Now he's slightly annoying. Cortana's sassiness irritates me in a way it didn't in the original. Jen Taylor is an amazing actress yet her performance is that of a Cortana from a completely different game. The Covenant also now speak English as well - why they decided to do this I have no idea. Tonally it's a mess, like a Zoomer directed the voice actors. 

Visually it's an incredible looking game, one of the few Unreal games that doesn't look like a typical Unreal game, though it's not very well optimised yet, but I'll admit my graphics card is a rather old one being a 3080. I won't say much about the gameplay because it's very good, however legendary difficulty is incredibly easy compared to the original. Far too easy.

Again, I can't emphasise enough how much they fumbled the tone of the story and dialogue. It's enough for me not to recommend the game. I couldn't stomach getting past the third level.

Oddly bad new voice direction, weirdly animated cutscenes that have a thoughtlessly fluid 'AI-ish' feeling to them, noticeable shimmering effect on most surfaces, no co-op matchmaking, and way too expensive for what's offered here. It's fun because of the same gameplay from the readily available and better-constructed Master Chief Collection. The best thing about this game is that it really makes you appreciate Halo Infinite

i was looking forward to this game and i knew going in that i wouldnt be having the best performance, but i had high hopes regardless. sadly on top of that the game is not as well optimized as it should be and the settings for graphics is almost non existent. i had to watch a video of how to lower the film grain in the games files to fix it (highest film grain i've ever seen in a game)

The only thing i can really find "good" about this game, is the graphics, the new way the Maw warthog drive is, and the newly designed flood missions. Other than that.... nothing else is really "good". The gun play is average. The gun sound design is off from what it used to be. this game hand holds WAY too much. "Hey these invisible might be too difficult for people to try and kill. lets put MARKERS over their heads so the players know where the camouflaged enemies are!". its just a two decade old reskinned game with lots of hand holding. Like cool, they added vehicle jacking, but the ruined the OG Magnum. i'd rather the magnum being the beast it was. i paid $100 (CAD)  for the early access premium edition of an old game thats missing HALF the content (ALL THE MULTIPLAYER IS GONE). i cannot justify this price tag for what you get when you could easily get Halo MCC with ALL the games for 50 bucks. thats base price mind you. This game is at best, 20 bucks. anything over is a rip off.

oh and P.S. apparently a lot of the code is just reused from other games. someone modded the reach jetback in easily since all the base code is still in the game.

This is a $50-70 Halo Reach mod pack that intentionally gutted the multiplayer suite in order to make the contextually lackluster and generic prequel missions. It's fun, like a mod pack, but mutually feels tacky as a result. And that's an insult to modern mod projects outdoing effort here slated for release soon (Ruby's Rebalanced Halo CE is a free and FANTASTIC revisit for folks wanting a CE tour, with Halo 2's right around the corner at the time of writing), alongside already released projects.

Your old friend may look the same, but the chemistry is gone. The conversations feel hollow and soulless. The laughters are forced. They keep talking more and more about politics. You keep waiting for the spark that made you enjoy their company years ago, but it never returns. You go home feeling more empty than when you first arrived. 

That’s how I felt playing through Halo’s campaign.

It seemed very cartoonish to me(minor spoiler over). Idgaf that Cortana is ugly. I do gaf that she looks and sounds wrong. Same with Johnson. I think most would agree that they nailed his look in H2A. This ain't it. Some of the cutscenes almost look like they're missing some sort of graphic effect or using a low quality texture. Feels really sloppy, and I imagine this wasn't supposed to be their final pass.

The remakes of the levels are actually fantastic; Especially missions 3, 5, 6, 7, and 8 are vastly improved by the streamlined level design. They just flow a lot better and downplay the copy paste that Bungie used for them. The AR slaps now, and behaves like more of a m…

Cons:
- The default elements which are getting shown on the HUD are really annoying. Thankfully you can turn most of them off. But how did anyone at 343 played and seen this and said: "Yes we ship it like this"

I'm a born halo fan, not a crazy one, but this game was decent, I don't regret buying it, but hope the voice actors do better in Halo 2.

This game is a mess. Between the outsourcing to reportedly about 15 different studios and it shows. Everything felt off about it, from the guns and the AI to the cutscenes. All throughout it for every moment that made me go "huh, that's neat" or "oh I don't mind that change", there were at least two more that made me question what the devs were thinking.
I'd go over all my problems but this would be multiple paragraphs. There were some cool additions, like hiding skulls throughout the levels and *some* of the cutscene changes, but overshadowed by damn near everything else.
Just get Halo Master Chief Collection. This isn't worth the $50

343/Halo Studios misses the mark again. Unreal Engine 5, the engine that they touted as being the thing that would refresh and revive Halo, ironically, is the thing that kills this game for me. The Slipspace Engine in Infinite ran so well, and had Infinite FEELING like Halo. Unreal Engine leaves Campaign Evolved feeling like its missing something. Every aspect of this game feels like a pulled punch. The music just isn't quite there. It's too quiet and lacks soul. It feels like they just used AI to make the score. The guns feel just not quite right. There is no oomf in the gunplay at all. The enemies' AI feels not quite there. There is no satisfaction in headshotting grunts and jackals. This game feels like there was no unifying vision. It feels like everything was outsourced to the cheapest labor. OH WAIT! IT WAS!

Unreal Engine 5 is all flash and no soul. Every single surface in this games is reflective and shiny, and every single particle effect is dialed up to 12. It makes this game incredibly difficult to run without tuning all your graphical settings down to Medium at minimum, and the sensory bombardment does little to hide what lies underneath. Campaign Evolved feels like a literal polished turd, except the polish makes the game not even playable. They gave this game the landlord special and just painted over all the rust and dirt with Unreal Engine 5's graphical choices. 343 decided they'd make a playable benchmarking program rather than a game. The input lag and stuttering this game has is inexcusable.

Was I excited for this? Yes. I was excited for a reboot where some of the choices Bungie made during Halo 1's development could be righted. Things like the Library, and the warthog run's infamous tiny bridge on the Pillar of Autumn. We received those things, but it came in a crusty cardboard box that they decided to paint gold and call a treasure.

I haven't beat this game yet. I will, and I will see if this review changes. If 343/Halo Studios likewise …

I'm disappointed.

When I looked back at the game, I realised that the only parts I enjoyed were the parts that were the OG Halo. My issues with this game are entirely everything that has been changed, and I'll list the worst ones.

- Forced Auto Aim, when I shoot at the hand of a jackal the game forces the bullets to curve into the middle of it's shield. Obnoxious.

- Inputs vanishing randomly, clicking to fire my gun randomly does nothing

- The Flood AI feel pathetic and slow, worse than Halo 3's which was already the weaker of the series.

- The AI switches off after 40 meters distance. They just stare at you while you shoot them down.

- The friendly AI is even more useless than Halo CE's, 5 sentinels can't even kill one flood

- The shotgun feels awful to use

- The new voicelines, dialogues and handholding just annoyed me. (Not played the new missions yet. Admittedly this might be nostalgia)

- Vehicle sensitivity is so bad, I had to turn my sensitivity up from 0.4 to 1.2 just to drive the scorpion properly

- The AI switches between oppressive (love it) and pathetic (just standing staring at you as you throw grenades)

- A lot of the guns feel weak, the needler being useless, the pistol sounding and being fairly weak, the shotgun being rough. The Assault Rifle is amazing other than the forced auto aim nonsense.

- They turned the Library into a series of wave based shooters instead of timed survival

- Characters randomly knowing lore and information they aren't meant to have yet

All they had to do was remake the original game and sand off the rough edges, improve some things (like Keyes dying resetting the mission, good job there) and bring halo forward a generation. If this is the best they can do with the literal mould already created for them, then I cannot have any faith in this development studio moving forward. If I want to play Halo CE, I'll play the MCC version.

Cons:
- The default elements which are getting shown on the HUD are really annoying. Thankfully you can turn most of them off. But how did anyone at 343 played and seen this and said: "Yes we ship it like this"
- The music doesn't fit in many areas or cutscenes. It feels like it's been placed completely at random.
- The dialogue has been changed significantly, and the voice acting feels unnatural. I'd even say some of it sounds AI-generated, especially if you play the game in any language other than English.
- The developers have added an artificial delay to basically everything (weapon switching, exiting vehicles, pressing buttons).
- The new Warthog controls are the worst I've ever experienced! Even PlayStation 1 games have better controls than this. Thankfully, you can switch back to the old driving scheme.
- The enemy AI feels extremely dumb. They fire a few shots and then fall back into their default animations.
- They got rid of the original Elite voice lines and replaced them with human speech (no more "WOOT WOOT WOOT").
- Somehow, the Library has become even worse (though I appreciate the effort).

I would advise any serious player to either play the original or the MCC version.

I came into this with an open mind hoping my concerns about the UE5 + Halo Studios combo weren't warranted.

Sadly, my concerns were more than warranted. Between myself and several other friends who I game with in VCs, we've had constant game crashes, softlocks in the prequel missions, and just poor optimization/stability in general.

The checkpoint system is horrendous and inaccurate. You can go 5+ minutes clearing out multiple rooms/areas without a checkpoint, and then all of a sudden, you'll get two checkpoints within five seconds of each other. Those checkpoints can often be when you're in combat as well.

Camo is completely broken. When you activate it, enemies will still know where you are a vast majority of the time, especially on legendary and LASO.

Enemy and friendly AI also breaks frequently throughout the campaign. Sometimes they can be stuck running into a wall like they're a Fallout 4 NPC, or sometimes they are just frozen and do nothing.

Sprint allows you to run past a vast majority of encounters, even on Legendary. It completely ruins the gameplay. 

To be clear, I'm not someone who cares a ton if a Halo game has sprint or not. What matters is how the level design fits the mechanics of the game. And whether it's the original Halo CE or the remake, it doesn't work. 

Percentage wise, Halo CE has more combat in close proximity compared to other Halos. When sprint was first brought into the franchise with Halo Reach, that campaign had way more missions and overall time spent in vehicles and in open spaces. There were also more enemies overall. So, you couldn't just sprint past most of the combat on Legendary (with a few exceptions of course).

But in Halo CE, in rooms or areas where you aren't required to kill every enemy, you can often just sprint past them since the enemy AI doesn't move quickly enough relative to how fast sprint is.

citations.review_text: No optimization at ALL done in this game. Its kinda crazy actually that they managed to ♥♥♥♥ up the performance that badly. DLSS is permanently ON and there's literally no way of disabling it. The graphics could've been better if not for DLSS and Lumen being active. Gunplay is fun, but not fun enough where it justifies this game's price. I regretted buying this game during the first hours of playing it, that should tell you enough.

[h1]My complete thoughts on the remake:[/h1]

Long-time Halo fan, been playing since the first game on the original Xbox. Do I think this game holds up to the original in comparison? Sadly, no. However, I do think this remake can serve as a good entry point for newer players, which now includes the PlayStation audience. It is a nice modernized FPS experience. I understand the need to switch to Unreal after what happened with the Slipspace Engine. The game looks great, Unreal Engine 5 looks as amazing as ever, but it's got all the little quirks of UE5 you've come to expect; poor optimization, poor performance, and high graphical demand. Also, no way to turn off DLSS/upscaling?

Some of the changes I like, I think they make more sense on a design/gameplay level, like the bridge on Assault on the Control Room/Two Betrayals. The lighting in 343 Guilty Spark looks perfect, the Library still feels like a slog, but the changes help it feel a little quicker, and the Warthog run on the Maw makes a little more sense with the ship being split open. Other changes, I'm not sure why they felt the need to do that: small changes like different music tracks at certain points, different items, differences in dialogue speakers, Elites speaking English, or things like the marines following you to Captain Keyes instead of staying behind and being killed. The Paranoid Marine doesn't even shoot at you anymore for some reason.

I'm struggling to see the artistic merit of this game. On the graphics side, there are some areas that leverage modern rendering and art to create striking imagery that exceed the original, but the ray tracing has poor temporal stability so reflective surfaces look like they're boiling. This shows up a lot and I find it very distracting. Most of the time I prefer the look of Combat Evolved.

For the gameplay, the changes to the levels range usually from minor to straight downgrades (I'm a self-admitted OG Library lover). Keyes is an exception and I really love what they did with it. The new voice acting is, in my opinion, far worse than the original, overwriting the original characterisation with an interpretation closer to Halo Infinite, which I don't care for. The prequel missions are terribly designed and very boring, with a pointless and forgettable story.

I would've said the remix mode, which randomises enemies and weapons, is a great addition, and I've had a lot of fun playing it in co-op, but I'm not able to complete one of the prequel missions whilst playing it because the trigger for Johnson opening a door won't fire. This, and various other bugs and annoyances, point to this being a poorly made piece of software - par for the course for this developer. It's honestly impressive how [strike] 343 Industries [/strike] Halo Studios managed to turn an exceptional game in Combat Evolved into a 6/10.

The bonus missions suck. They are just one kill room after another with bad writing and a dog fighting mission that bored me to tears. The CE campaign and the visuals are cool, but not 50 dollars cool. I'd say wait for a sale and skip the bonus missions if you do plan to get this game. It is fun, just not at all worth its price.

Great performance, $10, the only version of halo 1 with online competitive multiplayer, and a scoring and time system built in. These are things halo anniversary has that campaign evolved doesn’t. With no scoring system, I see no point in playing the campaign again other than achievement hunting. Between halo infinite and this is a 5 year wait and all this is is an asset drop. Copy pasted music, copy pasted enemies, even copy pasted sound effects, there’s nothing new in this game other than the 3 prequel missions that has nothing to do with the main campaign which they cut out multiplayer for. At least they added the beam rifle back which i like.

These cutscenes as well are an extreme downgrade from halo 2 anniversary cutscenes as well. many of the jackals and grunts do not move close to how they move in game and you can definitely tell its human movement instead of jackal or grunt movement.

Also a big selling point was the redo of the voice acting. 90% of the dialogue was a downgrade, the maw specifically. In the original “We’re not going to make it. Pull up, Pull up!!” you can hear the sense of panic cortana has that the banshee is falling apart but the new version sounds like they’re reading a script with no emotion behind it.

343, sorry HaLo StUdIoS, has consistently made worse and worse games, at least at launch, with this one, in my opinion, being my least favorite of the mainline games. Even though i do love the warthog run and the legendary ending, there is no way im wasting my time looking into halo 2 campaign evolved when halo 2 anniversary exists.

tldr: halo anniversary for the mcc is a much better deal

this remake of Halo:CE was just painful to sit through, once the couple hour honeymoon ended. the new missions were nothing notable, and only were there to pad out the content of this game, because they knew it wouldn't be enough to just release the campaign and call it there. oh, and no multiplayer, btw. why? I'm not huge on Halo's multiplayer, but it would have made this game more replayable, and this game desperately needs it . there is nothing in this "remake" that ever justifies the price tag, other then the graphics or maybe the gunplay, but that should be bare minimum for remakes. 

 just don't get this, even on sale, Just get the MCC Collection, at least you can play a better version of the game that came out 25 years ago. this is just nostalgia slop that they are selling to you for $50 (or more for the ♥♥♥♥♥♥ skins that don't justify the price or purpose).

I shouldn't be surprised at this point, but that's what I get for assuming they would make a good Halo game.

I am typically a positive review guy. I tend to look at what i enjoy about most games, and not so much at what i dont like. But, every dog has his day, and today is that day for this big dog.

I will start with what i liked and enjoyed:
- The game is beautiful. The UE5 graphics are at full display and breathes fresh life into a 25 year old game.
- It feels like modern halo. the gunplay is fun and satisfying. the sandbox is fun and interactive, just as i remember when i was younger.

Now, here are my problems:
- As it is currently, there are literally 0 achievement based skins to earn, or really anything other than steam achievements. To expect players to be satisfied with basically just playing the campaign over and over with nothing to work towards or play for, is just crazy. this is HALO and if they really wanted to reboot the franchise with the community in mind, then this should at least been near the top of things to include. major ball dropped.
- The lack of pvp multiplayer, in the big 2026, is actually a criminal offense. The most basic of basic game modes, like Team Deathmatch or a Free for All would have done just fine. Peer 2 Peer networking. EZPZ. But to not include anything with a supposed reboot of the franchise is unacceptable. Co-op will only last for so long before everyone is so bored they'd rather swallow a plasma cannon. I
- The game that is currently being presented feels like a giant corporate cash grab, and we already know halo 2 remastered is coming. If their main selling point is playing the campaign again in with a brand new coat of paint, even if it's incredibly beautiful, is just not enough. for the price, i find it ridiculous as to what's on offer.

Incredibly disappointing, Halo deserves better,

Please ignore the haters. 343 now Halo Studios deserves the criticism they have received from previous titles however this is not one of them. If you want a remaster you can play Master Chief Collection. This is a remake and is honestly better than I could have hoped for. I was a teen when Halo CE launched and it literally formed a new generation of gaming and community like we have never seen. 

The remake of the original story is fantastic and actually adds more context that all stays true to the original. The addition of more skulls, cosmetics and skins are also welcome to help bring Halo CE to new and returning players. The additional missions not from the original are not great but it's better than nothing. It still looks and feels like the original.

Play it for yourself and forget about the studios past. If you don't have a blast playing this then you never really liked the original to begin with.

Honestly, I don't know why this even exists... I mean I know its been 15 years since Anniversary but where people really asking for THIS rather than something like Halo 3 Anniversary?!?

Was this game with the £70 I paid? ABSOLUTELY NOT! 
Is it worth the normal price of £50, also NO!
In my opinion this is worth £30-£40 max!

I was annoyed straight away without even playing the game, I had to spend 20 mins just jumping through hoops trying to remember old emails and password recovery to my old Microsoft account, seriously why do I need to link an account to play a 25 year old campaign?

The 3 new missions with Temu Johnson... yeah I didn't care, I found them rather boring and they didn't add anything worthwhile, you and Temu Johnson infiltrate a covenant ship and fight your way to the bridge so you can download a map.... ok wooo exciting stuff I guess. But along the way you find a group of Marines and a ODST fighting for their lives trying to escape, you would think that the ODST trooper would be grateful that two of the most badass heroes in the UNSC suddenly showed up out of nowhere to pull them out of the fire, but no she's an insufferable girl boss who's got a chip on her shoulder about the chief for some reason... great modern writing.

Why is it in every Halo game the characters look so drastically different? I'm not a fan of this look for Cortana and her voice lines just sound terrible, same with Johnson, he looks like Steve Harvey cosplaying Johnson and his voice actor just doesn't have the same punch David Scully had and he pauses while delivering his lines way to often.

The inclusion of throwing in sprint and weapons from other games simply for the sake of it in my opinion takes away form the game's core identity, and all for the sake of appealing to the modern audience.

If you've never played Halo before then sure It's probably a good option for you If your wanting to experience Halo, but for long time fans like myself who are pulling on 25 years of nost…

As somepony who has 100%ed the game and gotten all the acheivements, i can say with certainty:
its just,, not great. save your money, play the original.
[h3]Pros:[/h3]
- Three new levels.* 
- New rooms in some levels.* 
- Redesigned library.*
- Looks beautiful.*
- Randomizer mode.*
- Lots of fun skulls!
- UE5 is easy to mod!
- New johnson is alright, you get used to him pretty quick 
[h3]Cons:[/h3]
- *One of the new levels suck, two are [b]just okay[/b].
- *The new rooms are cool, but dont add enough spice to break up the monotony of halo 1s levels.
- *The new library still sucks! it may look and play a little cooler but its still the library.
- *The visuals are nice, but you have a awful coat of Unreal 5 on it. its grainy, chromatic, ghosting mess of AI garbage upscaling and raytracing.
- *The randomizer mode is not nearly as interesting as youd think or want it to be.
- Weapon feel sucks and is a severe downgrade.
- Enemy AI is a severe downgrade.
- Cutscenes are cringe in a michael bay kinda way: "epic" camera angles and ♥♥♥♥♥♥ depth of field. I really liked H2As prerendered cutscenes, these ones suck and dont feel halo at all.
- New cortana lines are very "focus M."
- Enemy placement felt weird. 


[h2]Closing remarks[/h2]
This game is fine. Its alright even. But so is Halo Combat Evolved, which is 10USD, and comes in a 20USD collection with even more games. Buy and play that one.
